sources.entry: NeonLink - Bookmark service with unique design and simple installation with Docker. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: NeonLink is a lightweight, self-hosted bookmark service with tags, search, and automatic icon/title/description capture, installed mainly via Docker.
summary.what_it_does: NeonLink is a self-hosted bookmark manager described as simple, lightweight, and using minimal dependencies. It supports tags, search, and automatic fetching of each bookmark's icon, title, and description. It offers a customizable background and a dashboard, and it keeps data private on your own server. Installation is via a Docker image (alexscifier/neonlink) or a docker-compose.yml file, and the README says the images are optimized for Raspberry Pi. The app is built with React on the frontend and Fastify on the server, using SQLite via better-sqlite3 for storage.
use_cases: save and tag web links privately
run a bookmark dashboard on a Raspberry Pi
replace cloud bookmark services with a local one
how_to_run: edit docker-compose.yml and run: docker-compose up -d
notable: Designed to run on low-resource hardware, including Raspberry Pi (ARM v7 images)
Automatic icon, title, and description retrieval for bookmarks
Customizable background images mounted via Docker volume
caveats: README does not describe authentication or multi-user features
Development setup requires Node.js, npm, and fastify-cli; Windows development is recommended via git bash
